To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the isotopic record of the mammalian remains from La Paloma site (northern Iberia) does not show significant variations across the Magdalenian-Azilian sequence, pointing to prevalent and relatively constant local environmental conditions during the Late Glacial Maximum and the early Holocene.

(1) the La Paloma cave mammal record is characterized by stable and homogeneous stable isotope signatures across the stratigraphical sequence, (2) the isotopic signatures are compatible with the existence of C3 mixed woodland – mesic C3 grasslands in the study area, (3) the stable isotope signatures suggest the existence of an open habitat preference in the large Bovidae, (4) the stable isotopic signatures of horse are compatible with a mixed-feeding strategy

the isotopic data from the La Paloma cave site in Asturias (northern Spain) show no major changes in paleoclimatic conditions across the Magdalenian and Azilian sequences, pointing to a stable environment in this area of the northern Ibero-Armorican region.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the reconstruction of the paleoenvironmental and paleoclimatic conditions of northern Iberia during the late Quaternar, based on stable isotope data of mammalian remains from the archaeological site of La Paloma cave.

the reconstruction of the paleoenvironmental and climatic context of La Paloma Cave, a site of great archaeological relevance in the Iberian Peninsula, and its implications for human settlement and mobility during the Late Pleistocene.
the reconstruction of paleoclimatic and paleoecological conditions of the late Pleistocene in northern Iberia, based on the stable isotope analysis of mammalian remains from La Paloma (Asturias).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
La Paloma site was located in a relatively open landscape with a mixed C3/C4 vegetation, in a region with a relatively stable climate and hydrological conditions.
the La Paloma site was a refuge area for the local fauna during the Late Glacial, with the local community remaining stable throughout the whole sequence.
the paleoenvironmental context in northern Spain, during the last glacial–interstadial transition (~ 20,000–12,000 cal BP), was relatively stable and homogeneous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isotopic approach used in this study, based on the analysis of the mammalian record, is a powerful tool to reconstruct paleoclimatic and paleoenvironment conditions in the Iberian Peninsula.
the stable isotope record from La Palomacave suggests that the local mammalian community was able to adapt and survive the late Quaternarystochastic climatic and environmental dynamics.

, despite the synchrony of La Paloma with the global climatic events, the stable isotopic values from La Paloma suggest that the local conditions were stable and that there were no significant changes in vegetation cover and soil activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stable isotope approach can help in reconstructing paleoenvironmental and paleoclimatic conditions in a region where the paleontological and archaeological records are scarce.

the isotopic approach is a powerful tool to assess the paleoenvironmental context of archaeological sites, especially when the archaeological record is scarce or absent, as it is the case for the La Paloma site.

the La Paloma mammalian community structure and paleoecological conditions are consistent with the presence of a mosaic of habitats, with open areas interspersed with more forested environments, and with the existence of a mosaic of refugia for large herbivores, which could have been crucial for the survival and persistence of human groups in the northern Ibero-Armorican Peninsula.
